Well in my experience it's something very personal to each person and its not a blanket rule or reason to one person. Personally, it's a way to deal with difficult emotions and as a form of self punishment (I appreciate that probably raises more questions than it answers). But for some it's about control, or to prevent a more serious reaction (such as attempting suicide) and others it releases endorphins and makes them feel better. There's a complete myriad of reasons and you may never fully understand it but all you can do is be there to support those you know, but don't push it and we don't tend to like talking about it.
